subject: Anthropology
title: Supply Chains
description: A fast breakdown of Supply Chains for builders.

hook.text: Your phone has cobalt mined by children in Congo. Global supply chains connect consumers to suffering they never see.

buildup.text: Supply chains are the global networks that produce, transport, and deliver goods from raw materials to consumers.

discovery.text: Anna Tsing traced how matsutake mushrooms move from forest to market, revealing hidden labor and value at every step.

twist.text: Supply chains hide exploitation behind distance. The further the product travels, the more invisible the labor becomes.

climax.text: Understanding supply chains means tracing power. Who profits, who labors, and who pays the environmental cost?

punchline.text: Every product carries an invisible human cost.

quiz.question: What do supply chains often hide?
options: The exploitation and labor behind consumer goods

details.summary: Global supply chains connect producers and consumers across vast distances, obscuring the labor conditions and environmental impacts of production. Anthropologists trace these chains ethnographically, revealing the human costs hidden in everyday consumer goods.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding supply chains as social systems reveals the invisible labor, exploitation, and environmental destruction embedded in consumer products. This knowledge is essential for making supply chains more just and accountable.
takeaways: Supply chains obscure labor conditions and environmental impacts
Anthropologists trace these chains to reveal hidden human costs
Knowledge of supply chain realities enables accountability demands

faq.question: How do anthropologists study supply chains?
faq.answer: They conduct multi-sited ethnography, following commodities from production to consumption. An anthropologist might study cocoa farmers in Ghana, processors in the Netherlands, and chocolate consumers in the United States to trace how value is created, captured, and distributed.

faq.question: Why are supply chains an important topic for anthropology?
faq.answer: Supply chains are where global inequality is produced and reproduced daily. They connect wealthy consumers to impoverished producers through networks of power, exploitation, and environmental extraction that shape life chances for billions of people worldwide.
